title: Meter Reading from Photos
summary: Read kWh, kVAh and demand values from meter photos taken by readers or consumers, check them against what was keyed in, and route mismatches to billing staff before bills go out.

seo.title: AI Meter Reading from Photos for Utilities | VipraTech
seo.description: Computer vision that reads electricity, water and gas meter photos, checks readings and serial numbers, and flags mismatches before billing.

designed_for: Commercial or Billing Manager at a DISCOM

problem.intro: Where smart meters have not yet reached, meter readers visit each premises, key a reading into a spot billing app and take a photo of the display. Billing teams rarely have time to look at those photos, so wrong entries, reused images and provisional readings turn into disputed bills and complaint calls.

pain_points.title: Keyed readings that do not match the photo
pain_points.detail: A misread digit or a value from the wrong register produces a bill the consumer disputes and the utility later revises.

pain_points.title: Unusable and reused photos
pain_points.detail: Blurred, glare-covered or recycled photos mean nobody can check the reading when a complaint arrives.

pain_points.title: Provisional billing builds disputes
pain_points.detail: Door-locked and meter-not-accessible codes lead to average bills, which pile up into large corrections later.

pain_points.title: Tamper signs missed
pain_points.detail: Broken seals, burnt terminals and loose connections appear in photos but go unseen in high-volume billing cycles.

solution.overview: We build a photo verification service that sits between the meter reading app and the billing system. For each photo it locates the meter, reads the display or mechanical register, identifies which register is shown, such as kWh, kVAh or maximum demand, and reads the meter serial number. It checks timestamp and location against the consumer record, detects reused images and compares the reading with what the reader keyed in and with consumption history. Matching readings go to billing; mismatches and unreadable photos go to a supervisor queue. Visible tamper cues are passed to vigilance as leads for inspection, never as findings.
capabilities: Reads seven-segment LCD and LED displays and mechanical drum registers
Identifies the register shown, such as kWh, kVAh or maximum demand, on meters that cycle displays
Reads the meter serial number and matches it to the consumer master
Detects reused or duplicate photos and checks timestamp and geotag
Compares readings with the reader's entry and the consumer's consumption pattern
Lists visible tamper cues such as broken seals, damaged glass or burn marks for vigilance follow-up

workflow.title: Photo arrives from the reading app
workflow.detail: The reader's app sends the photo, keyed reading, status code, timestamp and GPS location.

workflow.title: Check photo quality and authenticity
workflow.detail: The service checks focus and glare, compares location with the consumer address and tests whether the image has been used before.

workflow.title: Read register and serial
workflow.detail: The display value, register type and serial number are read, each with a confidence score.

workflow.title: Compare and decide
workflow.detail: The reading is compared with the keyed value and consumption history, and matches above threshold are released.

workflow.title: Supervisor review
workflow.detail: Billing supervisors review mismatches, unreadable photos and tamper cues with the image beside the record.

workflow.title: Release or revisit
workflow.detail: Confirmed readings go to billing; the rest go to a revisit list or a vigilance inspection queue.

inputs: Meter photos with timestamp and GPS from the reading app
Consumer master with meter serial, category and location
List of meter makes and display types in the field
outputs: Machine-read value and register type with confidence
Mismatch and unreadable-photo flags for billing staff
human_in_the_loop: Billing supervisors decide every mismatch before a bill is generated. Tamper cues go to authorised inspection staff as leads; the system never raises an assessment or penalty on its own.
integrations: Spot billing or meter reading mobile app
Billing or CIS system such as SAP IS-U or an in-house platform
WhatsApp Business API for consumer self-reading
Meter data management system where smart meters coexist
guardrails: The reader's entry is never overwritten silently; differences always go to review
Tamper cues are leads for inspection, not evidence
Confidence thresholds set per meter type and display
Photos and location data retained only for the period your policy sets
Agency performance reports reviewed by managers before any action
compliance_notes: Consumer names, addresses and location data handled in line with the DPDP Act 2023.
Supports the accurate metering and billing expected under state supply codes and the Electricity (Rights of Consumers) Rules, 2020.

pilot.scope: Photos from one subdivision's billing cycle, processed in parallel with the current process so that no bill depends on the pilot.

faqs.q: Which meter types can it read?
faqs.a: Common single-phase and three-phase electronic meters with LCD or LED displays, older electromechanical meters with drum registers, and water and gas meters with dials or counters. During the pilot we tune on the makes and models in your service area.
Photos that are blurred, covered in glare or show the wrong object are flagged as unreadable instead of guessed. Reports by reader show where photo practice needs attention.

faqs.q: Can consumers submit their own readings?
faqs.a: Yes. A WhatsApp self-reading flow can accept a meter photo, read it and confirm the value back to the consumer, with the same checks before it reaches billing.

faqs.q: Do we have to change our reading app?
faqs.a: Usually not. The service exposes an API your app vendor can call, or it can pick up photos from the storage your app already uses.
